solution: Evaluate both determinants. The left side is \(\begin{vmatrix} x & 2 \\ 18 & x \end{vmatrix} = x^2 - 36\). The right side is \(\begin{vmatrix} 6 & 2 \\ 18 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = 36 - 36 = 0\). So \(x^2 - 36 = 0\), giving \(x = \pm 6\). Hence (B).

A determinant equals the sum of the products of the elements of any one row (or column) with their own cofactors. Expanding along the first column gives \(\Delta = a_{11} A_{11} + a_{21} A_{21} + a_{31} A_{31}\). (Options A and C mix elements with the cofactors of a different row/column — those alien-cofactor sums are \(0\).) Hence (D).
For a nonsingular square matrix of order \(n\), \(|\operatorname{adj} A| = |A|^{n-1}\). Here \(n = 3\), so \(|\operatorname{adj} A| = |A|^{2}\). Hence (B).
Since \(A A^{-1} = I\), taking determinants gives \(\det(A)\det(A^{-1}) = \det(I) = 1\). Therefore \(\det(A^{-1}) = \dfrac{1}{\det(A)}\). Hence (B).

For a diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries, the inverse is the diagonal matrix of the reciprocals: \(A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} x^{-1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & y^{-1} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & z^{-1} \end{bmatrix}\) (check: \(A A^{-1} = I\)). Hence (A).
